title: Session placement topology and migration decision log
body:
Meeting: Architecture review — session placement topology & live migration
Date: 2026-03-10
Attendees: Ava Chen (owner), Miguel Torres, Priya Sharma, Ethan Park, Liam Nguyen, Sofia Becker

Purpose:
- Review proposed session placement topology for multi-variant routing and live migration strategies for stateful conversations.
- Surface failure modes, operational costs, and rollout plan for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Agenda:
1) Quick recap of constraints and goals (5m)
2) Topology proposals and tradeoffs (30m)
3) State transfer/migration protocol options (20m)
4) Observability & SLO implications (15m)
5) Decisions and action items (10m)

Recap (constraints & goals):
- Goal: minimize 99th and tail latencies for conversational workloads while enabling non-disruptive migration between host pools (eg. autoscaling, reserved maintenance, upgrade rollouts).
- Must support: session affinity, cross-model fallbacks, and multi-variant routing.
- Deploy modes: hosted API (fastest path), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC/on-prem where network constraints and slower cross-host transfers are expected).
- Important non-functional: deterministic and predictable cost impact, bounded consistency window during migration, and easy rollback for canary model/infra changes.

Topology proposals reviewed:
A) Deterministic hashed placement (coarse slots):
- Each tenant session -> deterministic hash to N placement slots. Each slot is assigned to a host group (pool).
- Pros: simple affinity, easy to reason about routing, cheap routing table.
- Cons: large data movement if slot-to-host mapping changes; rebalancing requires migrating many sessions at once unless sharded slots.

B) Two-tier placement (hot-worker + cold-store):
- Keep active KV/cache/kv-cached state on a hot worker; cold session snapshots live in a distributed blob store. Router can route to hot worker when active; otherwise route to a rehydration worker that fetches snapshot.
- Pros: reduced memory pressure on workers, faster eviction, lower steady-state cost.
- Cons: rehydration latency spike, more complex eviction/TTL management, storage cost and egress in Private.

C) Lease-based slot assignment with graceful handoff orchestrator (recommended hybrid):
- Each slot has a lease owner (worker). Lease expiration + proactive handoff window. Migration orchestrator coordinates transfer: live delta sync (incremental KV diffs) then switch routes after final flush.
- Pros: fine-grained movement, supports incremental rebalancing, can enforce bounded consistency windows.
- Cons: more moving pieces (lease protocol, orchestrator), requires reliable inter-host RPC for delta syncs and backpressure handling.

State transfer / migration protocol alternatives:
1) Stop-the-world snapshot + restore:
- Easiest to implement; take full snapshot, move, restore.
- Too disruptive for low-latency apps. OK for maintenance windows in Private only.

2) Shadow-copy + cutover (recommended for Hosted/Dedicated):
- Start a shadow instance on target host; replicate all writes (or KV deltas) for session since shadow creation; when delta backlog is < threshold, switch router to target and let source gracefully retire.
- This minimizes cutover window and preserves existing KV caches. Works well with deterministic routing fallback.

3) On-demand rehydrate (for Two-tier option):
- Let new host rehydrate from blob store on first request, accept initial latency spike; use TTL to limit frequency.
- Use for low-activity sessions and batch migration.

Observability & SLO implications discussed:
- Must measure: migration-time tail latency (p95/p99), delta backlog size, transfer throughput (MB/s), number of sessions in-flight, and failed transfers.
- Add explicit migration telemetry tags: migration_id, source_host, target_host, session_id, migration_phase.
- SLO policy: migrations should not increase 99th token latency by more than 15% for affected customers; emergency abort if >30% for >60s.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Partial transfer (target missing some keys): require final integrity check (checksum over active keys) before cutover; fallback to source if checksum fails.
- Network interruptions mid-sync: orchestrator retries with exponential backoff; if backlog grows past threshold, automatically abort and reschedule during low load window.
- Misrouted requests during cutover: router implements short-lived dual-write window and a short sticky session grace to retry on both hosts for a few seconds.
- Private deployments with restricted outbound: fall back to snapshot restore and scheduled maintenance migration (longer windows) — document in Private deployment runbook.

Cost estimation notes (rough):
- Shadow-copy approach increases transient memory and network egress. Expected additional 0.5–1.5% of hourly GPU/network cost during steady rebalances on medium clusters; can spike to 5–8% during large rebalances.
- Two-tier reduces worker memory cost at expense of persistent storage (S3 or similar) and occasional rehydration egress.

Decision summary (consensus):
- Adopt hybrid approach: lease-based slot assignment + shadow-copy delta replication for live migration in Hosted/Dedicated.
- For Private: provide a configurable mode: either shadow-copy (if networking permitted) or scheduled snapshot-and-restore for air-gapped/low-bandwidth setups.
- Implement migration orchestrator as a control-plane service with explicit migration records and abort/resume capabilities.
- Router changes: support short dual-write window and migration-aware routing table with sticky grace TTL.
- Observability: implement migration-specific metrics and an alert when migration backlog > configured threshold for >2 minutes.

Open questions (actionable):
- Q1: Exact delta format and compression strategy for incremental KV diffs — binary + optional zstd? (owner: Miguel; due: 2026-03-19)
- Q2: Migration orchestration API contract for Private deployments where control plane cannot reach hosts — how to coordinate? (owner: Priya; due: 2026-03-22)
- Q3: Canary rollout policy for orchestrator itself (how many concurrent migrations allowed by default?) — define safe defaults. (owner: Ethan; due: 2026-03-17)
- Q4: Backpressure interaction between migration network transfer and normal inference traffic — need cap strategy and throttling. (owner: Liam; due: 2026-03-18)

Action items & owners:
- Miguel: prototype delta serialization + compression benchmark (zstd vs snappy) against typical KV payload shapes (textual embeddings, small context blobs). Report: 2026-03-19.
- Priya: draft Private migration runbook options and required config flags for on-prem installs; include network pre-reqs and maintenance window template. Draft: 2026-03-22.
- Ethan: design migration orchestrator API (start/abort/resume/status) + safety knobs (max concurrent migrations, per-host throttle). PR: initial sketch by 2026-03-17.
- Liam: run a synthetic load test to surface worst-case latency during shadow-copy for 100k sessions; produce dashboard mockups and threshold recommendations. Deliverable: 2026-03-24.
- Sofia: update router design doc to include dual-write window semantics, routing TTLs, and sticky session fallback logic. Target: 2026-03-20.

Rollout plan (high-level):
1) Implement migration orchestrator skeleton + router read-only support for migration records (canary in staging).
2) Prototype delta sync plugin and telemetry; run cluster-sized load tests.
3) Canary in hosted (low traffic subset), monitor p95/p99 and cost metrics, iterate on throttles.
4) Add Private-compatible mode and runbook; validate with partner on-prem lab.

Notes & references:
- Related tickets: JIRA-RI-8765 (session-affinity redesign), JIRA-RI-8790 (migration telemetry), JIRA-RI-8812 (private-runbook).
- Prototype code: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/429 (initial lease plan + orchestrator sketch).
- Prior art: referenced redis-raft live migration papers and link to confluence summary (CONFLUENCE-1234).

Appendix (quick strawman parameters):
- delta-backlog-threshold: 64MB
- migration-cutover-window-target: <200ms added p99 token latency
- max-concurrent-migrations-per-cluster: 200 (configurable)
- dual-write-grace: 5s sticky retries

Meeting notes taken by: Ava Chen
Next sync: review prototypes and answers to open questions on 2026-03-25 (standup + deep-dive).

Tone: working doc — expect edits and follow-ups.
